expectation: `orderedDestinationGroups` passes the `Map` returned by `groupByDestination` to `orderManifestGroups`, whose comparator reads a `destination` field that the `[key, group]` entries lack, so the groups keep insertion order instead of ascending lexical order.
finding: `orderedDestinationGroups` passes the `Map` returned by `groupByDestination(records)` directly to `orderManifestGroups`. Spreading the `Map` yields `[key, group]` tuples whose `.destination` property is `undefined`, so the comparator always returns `0` and leaves entries in insertion order rather than ascending lexical order.

requirementSource.requirement: `orderedDestinationGroups` returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.

expectation: The geocoder contract defines `geocoder.lookup` only for known addresses, so it cannot be established whether an unknown address resolves to `undefined` (left out), resolves to another value (kept) or rejects (the whole call rejects).
finding: `locateStops` awaits `geocoder.lookup(stop.address)` in `Promise.all` and filters `stop.point !== undefined`, but `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md` specifies `geocoder.lookup(address)` only for known addresses and does not define whether unknown addresses resolve to `undefined`, resolve to `null`, or reject.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md`, `locateStops` leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.

expectation: `withinVehicleCapacity` converts the limit to grams and requires the clamped remainder to be above zero, so a total equal to the limit (remainder 0) is rejected.
finding: `withinVehicleCapacity(weight, limit)` checks `remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0`. When `weight` in grams equals `limit * 1000` (the configured limit in kilograms), `remainingVehicleCapacity` returns `0` and `0 > 0` returns `false`, rejecting a total equal to the configured limit.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `withinVehicleCapacity` accepts a total equal to the configured limit.

expectation: `canPlanRoute` checks `routes:admin` in the actor's own scopes instead of its held scopes, so an admin scope held through an active claim does not meet the ownership requirement.
finding: Under rules 3-4 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, an actor's held scopes include active claims as well as `actor.scopes`, and holding `routes:admin` satisfies depot ownership for every depot. `canPlanRoute` checks `actor.scopes.includes('routes:admin')` instead of `effectiveScopes(actor, now).includes('routes:admin')`, rejecting actors who hold `routes:admin` via an active claim.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` treats an actor holding `routes:admin` as owning every depot.

expectation: `effectiveScopes` drops only the actor's own scopes when it is suspended and still adds active-claim scopes, so a suspended actor with an active `routes:plan` claim can plan.
finding: Under rule 5 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` (which overrides rule 4), a suspended actor has no held scopes. `effectiveScopes` omits `actor.scopes` when `actor.suspended === true` but still appends active claim scopes, allowing a suspended actor with an active `routes:plan` claim and depot ownership (or `routes:admin` in `actor.scopes`) to pass `canPlanRoute`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` refuses every suspended actor.

expectation: `handleAnnouncementFailure` removes the copy returned by `store.get`, and `store.remove` removes only the exact stored object, so the stored manifest is not removed.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `store.get(id)` returns a new copy of the stored manifest while `store.remove(manifest)` removes a stored manifest only when given that exact stored object. On announcement failure, `handleAnnouncementFailure` passes `current = await store.get(manifest.id)` (a copy) to `store.remove(current)` instead of `manifest`, so `store.remove` removes nothing.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `publishWithAnnouncement` removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.

expectation: `stripCredentials` recurses only into values whose constructor is `Object`, so credentials inside arrays below `auth` are kept.
finding: Under rules 23-24 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `token`, `secret`, and `password` fields must be removed at every depth. `stripCredentials` only recurses when `value?.constructor === Object`, leaving credentials inside arrays or null-prototype objects nested below `event.auth` unredacted.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `redactManifestEvent` removes every credential nested below an `auth` field.

expectation: `buildManifest` copies each record shallowly and `labelDriver` assigns the label onto the supplied driver object, so supplied records are mutated.
finding: `buildManifest` shallow-copies each `record` but calls `labelDriver(record.driver)`, which executes `Object.assign(driver, {label: preserveManifestDriver(driver.label)})` and mutates `record.driver` in place on the supplied record.

requirementSource.requirement: `buildManifest` copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.

expectation: `publishManifest` maps entries through an async callback, and every resulting promise is truthy, so a manifest with invalid entries is stored.
finding: `publishManifest` maps entries with an `async` callback (`manifest.entries.map(async entry => manifestEntryIsValid(entry))`), producing an array of `Promise` objects that are always truthy under `checks.every(Boolean)`, so invalid manifests are still stored via `stageManifest`.

requirementSource.requirement: `publishManifest` stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.

expectation: `asPublicationError` marks a failure transient when it has a finite `retryAfter` even if it is marked `transient: false`, so `publishWithRetry` retries a failure rule 27 makes non-transient.
finding: Under rule 27 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` (which overrides rule 26), a failure marked `transient: false` is never transient even if it carries a finite numeric `retryAfter`. `asPublicationError` sets `transient: error?.transient === true || Number.isFinite(error?.retryAfter)`, causing `publishWithRetry` to retry failures marked `{transient: false, retryAfter: 1}`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `publishWithRetry` retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.

expectation: The public dispatch entry omits the executor surface.
finding: `src/dispatch/index.mjs` re-exports planning, capacity, access, schedule, retry, serialization, storage, manifest, publisher, and telemetry modules, but omits `./executor.mjs` and `dispatchRoute` from `./runtime.mjs`, so dispatch execution operations are not connected through the public dispatch entry.

requirementSource.requirement: Connect dispatch planning and execution through the public dispatch entry.

expectation: `coalesceAcrossGroups` records raw package IDs but filters normalized IDs, so a duplicate that differs only in surrounding whitespace survives in a later group.
finding: `coalesceAcrossGroups` filters trimmed IDs from `normalizePackageIds(group.packageIds)` against `seen`, but adds the raw untrimmed `group.packageIds` entries to `seen`. When an earlier group has an untrimmed ID such as `' P1 '`, `'P1'` is not added to `seen` and duplicate `'P1'` IDs remain in subsequent groups.

requirementSource.requirement: `coalescePackages` removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.

expectation: `nextRetryDelay` tests `retryAfter` by truthiness, so a server-provided `retryAfter` of 0 falls back to the computed backoff instead of a 0 ms delay.
finding: `nextRetryDelay` branches on truthiness (`retryAfter ? ...`) instead of checking for a finite numeric `retryAfter` as required by Retry timing rule 7: when `retryAfter` is `0`, it ignores `0` and falls back to `computeBackoff(attempt)`, and when `retryAfter` is a truthy non-finite or non-numeric value such as `'soon'` or `Infinity`, it calls `retryAfterDelay(retryAfter)` instead of `computeBackoff(attempt)`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `nextRetryDelay` applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided `retryAfter`.

expectation: `executeAuthorizedPlan` awaits dispatch as an argument of `unlessForbidden`, so dispatch runs before the authorization result is applied.
finding: `executeAuthorizedPlan` evaluates `await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route)` as an argument to `unlessForbidden(...)` before `unlessForbidden` checks `canPlanRoute(actor, route, now)`, invoking `dispatch(route)` even when the caller is unauthorized.

requirementSource.requirement: `executeAuthorizedPlan` rejects an unauthorized caller before invoking dispatch.

expectation: `stopsForDriver` compares each stop's own `driver`, so a stop with a `reassignment` is returned for its original driver and not for the driver of its `reassignment`, which rule 30 makes its assigned driver.
finding: Under rule 30 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop's assigned driver is `stop.reassignment.driver` when the stop has a `reassignment` and otherwise `stop.driver`, but `stopsForDriver` checks only `stop.driver === driver` and ignores `stop.reassignment`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `stopsForDriver` returns exactly the stops whose assigned driver is the given driver.

expectation: `chooseDeparture` moves a blackout departure to the blackout end hour without refusing it when that hour is outside the departure window.
finding: Under rule 14 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a departure chosen inside the departure window (`2..4` UTC) and then moved outside it by blackout adjustment (`3..5` UTC, moving to hour `5`) must be refused, but `chooseDeparture` returns `atUtcHour(date, 5)` without checking that the adjusted hour remains within `departureWindow`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `chooseDeparture` applies every Departure timing rule.

expectation: No available contract establishes when `store.write` invokes `onCommit`, so it cannot be established that `plan.created` is emitted only after storage succeeds.
finding: `emitPlanCreated` passes `onStored: () => emitter.emit('plan.created', input.plan.id)` into `savePlan`, which delegates to `store.write(plan, {onCommit: onStored})`. Neither `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md` nor any repository module specifies the contract for `store.write` or when `onCommit` is invoked, so post-storage emission cannot be verified.

requirementSource.requirement: `emitPlanCreated` emits `plan.created` only after storage succeeds.

expectation: `hasDuplicateRouteKeys` concatenates the depot ID and normalized route key without a separator, so different route identities can produce the same key.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `hasDuplicateRouteKeys` reports duplicates exactly when two stops are duplicates.

expectation: `parseRetryCount` converts text with `Number`, so text that is not base-10 digits, such as `'0x2'`, `'2e0'`, `' 2'` or `''`, is accepted as a retry count.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `parseRetryCount` accepts exactly the valid retry counts and otherwise returns an error result.

expectation: A failure marked `transient: false` that carries a finite `retryAfter` is rewrapped as transient, so publication retries do not stop for it.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:46`: under rule 27 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` (overriding rule 26), a failure marked `transient: false` is never transient even with a finite numeric `retryAfter`, yet `asPublicationError` marks it `transient: true` and `publishWithRetry` retries instead of stopping immediately.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, publication retries stop immediately for failures that the Failure classification rules do not make transient.

expectation: A suspended actor keeps the scopes of its active claims in `effectiveScopes`, so `canPlanRoute` can still allow it.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:51`: under rule 5 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a suspended actor has no held scopes, but `effectiveScopes` still includes active claim scopes when `actor.suspended === true`, allowing a suspended actor with an active `routes:plan` claim and depot ownership (or `routes:admin` in `actor.scopes`) to pass `canPlanRoute`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a suspended actor cannot plan any route.

expectation: Delivery notices are sent to the raw `phone`, so an entry whose `phone` contains spaces or hyphens is not notified at its contact phone (rule 33).
finding: Under rule 33 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, an entry's contact phone is its `phone` with every space (` `) and hyphen (`-`) character removed, but `sendDeliveryNotices` calls `sms.send(entry.phone, ...)` with the raw `entry.phone` value.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, delivery notices go to the contact phone of every manifest entry.

expectation: Route duration adds the raw `serviceMinutes`, so every stop misses the 5 minutes of parking that rule 32 includes in its service time.
finding: Under rule 32 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop's service time is `serviceMinutes` plus 5 minutes of parking, but `routeDuration` sums only `stop.travelMinutes + stop.serviceMinutes` and omits the 5 parking minutes per stop.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.

expectation: A server-provided `retryAfter` of 0 is falsy, so `nextRetryDelay` uses the computed backoff instead of the server delay.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:19`: `nextRetryDelay` tests truthiness (`retryAfter ? ...`) rather than finite numeric `retryAfter`, falling back to `computeBackoff(attempt)` when `retryAfter` is `0` and calling `retryAfterDelay(retryAfter)` on truthy non-finite or non-numeric values.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next retry delay follows the Retry timing rules whenever the server provides `retryAfter`.

expectation: Manifest-event redaction leaves arrays unvisited, so a credential in an object inside an array of the authentication data is not removed.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:23`: under rules 23-24 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `token`, `secret`, and `password` fields must be removed at every depth, but `stripCredentials` only recurses when `value?.constructor === Object`, leaving credentials inside arrays or null-prototype objects nested inside `event.auth` unredacted.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.

expectation: The announcement failure branch passes the new copy from `store.get` to `store.remove`, which removes nothing for any object other than the stored one.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:22`: under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `store.get(id)` returns a new copy while `store.remove(manifest)` removes a stored manifest only when given that exact stored object; `handleAnnouncementFailure` passes `current = await store.get(manifest.id)` to `store.remove(current)`, so rollback removes nothing.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.

expectation: Package coalescing compares normalized IDs against raw IDs seen in earlier groups, so whitespace variants of one ID are kept across groups.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:48`: `coalesceAcrossGroups` filters normalized (trimmed) package IDs against `seen` but records raw untrimmed `group.packageIds` in `seen`, leaving duplicate normalized package IDs across destination groups when earlier IDs had surrounding whitespace.

requirementSource.requirement: Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.

expectation: After `renameTemporary` rejects, the temporary bytes are locked, so the `discardTemporary` call in `writePlanAtomically` only closes the write and keeps them; `removeTemporary` is never called.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, when `store.renameTemporary()` rejects, the temporary bytes stay in place and are locked, and while locked `store.discardTemporary()` keeps the bytes whereas `store.removeTemporary()` deletes locked bytes. `writePlanAtomically` calls `store.discardTemporary()` on rename failure, leaving the locked temporary bytes in place.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.

expectation: `canAssignAllPackages` delegates to `withinVehicleCapacity`, whose remaining-capacity test is false at zero remainder, so a total equal to the limit is rejected.
finding: `canAssignAllPackages` delegates to `withinVehicleCapacity(totalPackageWeight(packages), limit)`, which checks `remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0`. When total package weight in grams equals `limit * 1000` (the vehicle limit in kilograms), `remainingVehicleCapacity` is `0` and `0 > 0` returns `false`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, assigning all packages accepts a total equal to the vehicle limit.

expectation: The public entry does not export `executor.mjs`.
finding: `src/dispatch/index.mjs` omits `./executor.mjs` (`executeAuthorizedPlan`, `executeDryRun`, `planFailure`, `runEligibleStops`, `emitPlanCreated`, `pendingStops`) and `dispatchRoute` from `./runtime.mjs`, so callers cannot import execution operations from the public dispatch entry.

requirementSource.requirement: The public dispatch entry exports the execution operations used by callers.

expectation: Plan serialization sorts only the top-level keys (`withSortedKeys` proxies only the plan object), so nested objects keep their insertion order and plans that differ only in nested field order hash to different values.
finding: `checksumPlan` hashes `serializePlan(plan)`, which uses `withSortedKeys(plan)`. `withSortedKeys` only wraps the top-level object in a `Proxy` sorting top-level `ownKeys` and does not sort keys of nested objects, so differing field order inside nested objects produces different serialized JSON and different plan hashes.

requirementSource.requirement: Two plans that differ only in the order of the fields inside their nested objects have the same plan hash.

expectation: Urgent-stop partitioning tests the raw `priority` for the remaining partition, so a text priority such as `'7'` (priority 5 under rule 15) is placed in no partition.
finding: Under rules 15-16 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop without a finite numeric `priority` has priority `5` (not urgent). `partitionUrgentStops` filters `urgent` with `priorityOf(stop) > 5` but filters `remaining` with `!(stop.priority > 5)`, so stops with `priority: Infinity` or `priority: '10'` are excluded from both `urgent` and `remaining`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, urgent-stop partitioning places every stop in exactly one partition according to its urgency.

finding: Under rule 32 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop's service time is `serviceMinutes` plus 5 minutes of parking, but `routeDuration` sums only `stop.travelMinutes + stop.serviceMinutes` and omits the 5 parking minutes per stop.

problemOptions.expectation: Route duration adds the raw `serviceMinutes`, so every stop misses the 5 minutes of parking that rule 32 includes in its service time.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.

finding: Under rule 10 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, all departure hours are UTC hours, but `nextDispatchTime` checks `isWithinBlackout(candidate.getHours(), departureWindow.blackout)` using the local-timezone hour `getHours()` instead of `getUTCHours()`.

problemOptions.expectation: `nextDispatchTime` checks the blackout with the host-local hour instead of the UTC hour, so on a non-UTC host a time inside the blackout is not moved.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.

finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:28`: `emitPlanCreated` passes `onStored` into `savePlan`, which passes `{onCommit: onStored}` to `store.write(plan, {onCommit: onStored})`, and no repository or adapter contract specifies `store.write` or when `onCommit` runs.

problemOptions.expectation: Plan-created telemetry depends on when the store invokes `onCommit`, which no available contract defines.

requirementSource.requirement: Plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds.

finding: Under rule 18 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop without a finite numeric `sequence` must follow every stop of equal priority that has one. `compareStops` uses `(left.sequence ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) - (right.sequence ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)`, which fails to place non-nullish non-finite sequences such as `-Infinity`, `NaN`, or `'none'` (or nullish sequences compared against finite numbers above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) after finite numeric sequences.

problemOptions.expectation: The stop comparator coerces a text `sequence` such as `'2'` to a number, so a stop without a finite numeric sequence does not follow the equal-priority stops that have one.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.

finding: `authorizeRouteBatch` computes `firstRejected = routes.findIndex(route => !requireDepotOwner(actor, route))` and returns `firstRejected <= 0`. When the first route (`index 0`) fails `requireDepotOwner`, `firstRejected` is `0` and `0 <= 0` returns `true` instead of rejecting the batch.

problemOptions.expectation: `authorizeRouteBatch` accepts the batch when `findIndex` returns 0, so a batch whose first route fails depot ownership is authorized.

requirementSource.requirement: Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.

finding: Under rule 28 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, recorded package weights must be in grams. `weighPackages` stores `await scale.read(entry.packageId)` without conversion, and `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md` does not specify the measurement unit returned by `scale.read(packageId)`.

problemOptions.expectation: The weighing contract does not state the unit of the weight that `scale.read` resolves to, so it cannot be established that weighed package weights are in grams.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, package weighing records each package weight in the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.

finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:20`: `executeAuthorizedPlan` evaluates `await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route)` before `unlessForbidden` checks `canPlanRoute(actor, route, now)`, invoking `dispatch(route)` for unauthorized callers.

requirementSource.requirement: Authorized execution rejects a caller before invoking dispatch.
